title: Anticoagulant Cessation After Antiphospholipid Autoantibodies Loss in Thrombotic Antiphospholipid Syndrome
off: A Randomised Controlled Trial to Evaluate Anticoagulant Cessation After Antiphospholipid Autoantibodies Loss in Thrombotic Antiphospholipid Syndrome
collabs: Direction Générale de l'Offre de Soin (DGOS)

officials.a: Assistance Publique - Hôpitaux de Paris (AP-HP), Hôpital Bichat, Department of Internal Medicine

summary: This is an open-label, non-inferiority, randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (experimental and control), following a PROBE (Prospective Randomized Open, Blinded Endpoint) design. The study evaluates whether anticoagulation cessation is non-inferior to anticoagulation maintenance regarding the risk of recurrent thrombosis after antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) loss in patients with thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). Currently, the cornerstone of APS treatment is long-term anticoagulation by vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), which expose patients to the risk of bleeding and have a negative impact on health-related quality of life due to the need for frequent International Normalized Ratio (INR) monitoring. No clinical trial in the existing literature has evaluated anticoagulant cessation after aPL loss. The primary endpoint is the first recurrent thrombotic event during follow-up.
desc:
The most frequent clinical manifestations of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) are thrombotic events. The specificities of antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL), their isotypes, and the presence of multiple aPL autoantibodies have been associated with different risk profiles regarding thrombotic manifestations, while the risk of thrombotic events after disappearance of aPL appears to decrease. Currently, no clinical trial in the existing literature has evaluated anticoagulant cessation after aPL loss.

At the randomisation visit, demographic, medical, and biological characteristics are collected and the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) questionnaire is completed. Follow-up visits are scheduled every 3 months for the first 6 months (M3, M6), then every 6 months for a minimum of 18 months and a maximum of 42 months (M12 through M48). In the experimental arm, International Normalized Ratio (INR) testing is performed at baseline then discontinued; in the control arm, INR is monitored at baseline, at each protocol visit, in case of recurrent thrombotic event, and as clinically indicated. Serum and plasma samples are collected at baseline, at each follow-up visit, and in case of recurrent thrombotic event, for centralized aPL antibody measurement and biocollection.

The study was designed to demonstrate non-inferiority based on a 2-year outcome rate of 20% in the anticoagulant cessation group and 17% in the anticoagulation maintenance group. A total of 234 patients is required to reject the non-inferiority null hypothesis with 80% power, a one-sided type I error rate of 2.5%, and a non-inferiority margin of 10%. The primary endpoint will be analyzed in both intention-to-treat (ITT, primary analysis) and per-protocol (PP) populations. Between-group comparisons will use an appropriate statistical model (e.g., logistic regression, linear models, or Cox proportional hazards models), with treatment effect estimated together with its two-sided 95% confidence interval. Sensitivity analyses will be conducted to assess the robustness of the primary results, and missing data will be handled according to prespecified methods.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Adults ≥ 18 years old
2. Signed written consent form
3. Primary or secondary thrombotic APS according to 2023 ACR/EULAR classification criteria
4. aPL antibodies loss of LA, aCL, and aβ2GPI antibodies - defined as a normalised level (\< 99th percentile) - in at least two consecutive measurements with at least 12 months between each measurement including one negative measurement within the 3 months preceding inclusion
5. Long term (\>12 months) VKAs therapy

Exclusion Criteria:

1. History of severe venous thrombosis. Severe venous thrombosis including massive pulmonary embolism; chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension; hepatic, mesenteric, renal and/or cerebral venous thrombosis
2. History of arterial thrombosis
3. History of recurrent venous thrombosis while receiving VKAs
4. History of catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (CAPS)
5. Triple aPL positivity
6. Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 for each VKAs medicinal product
7. Malignant hypertension
8. Severe hepatic impairment
9. Active malignancy
10. Presence of a mechanical heart valve or any other medical condition requiring anticoagulation with a VKA
11. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
12. Subject deprived of freedom, subject under a legal protective measure
13. No affiliation to any health insurance system
14. Enrolment to another interventional study (clinical trial on medicinal product, medical device and interventional research involving human participants not concerning health product)

arms.d: Participants in this arm discontinue vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy at the randomisation visit. Anticoagulant treatment duration in this arm is 0 month. International Normalized Ratio (INR) testing is performed at baseline (M0) and then discontinued. Participants are followed according to the study visit schedule (M3, M6, then every 6 months up to M48), with clinical and biological assessments including antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) measurement, and are restarted on anticoagulant therapy only in case of a recurrent thrombotic event.

Participants in this arm continue vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy (fluindione, warfarin, or acenocoumarol), dosed orally to obtain an International Normalized Ratio (INR) between 2 and 3, for a minimum of 24 months (up to 48 months depending on time of enrollment). INR is monitored at baseline (M0), at M3, at each subsequent protocol visit, in case of recurrent thrombotic event, and as clinically indicated. Participants are also followed with clinical and biological assessments including antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) measurement. Participants follow the same visit schedule as the experimental arm (M3, M6, then every 6 months up to M48)
